blocking.issue: SLO-GW-4 claims a tie to SM-6, but the two measure different things. SM-6 in Vision and positioning is the WASM Plugin Phase call overhead from a per-Phase microbenchmark. The SLI of SLO-GW-4 is `ruralz_plugin_call_duration_seconds`, which the catalog defines as the whole Plugin call, guest work included. Configuration model Plugins may run up to their `limits.timeout` (5 ms for `geo-block`), so the SLO would page on correct Plugins. The Performance Budget for SM-6 also cannot be "the lab ceiling on the same metric" (line 410).
blocking.evidence: Line 417: "| SLO-GW-4 | `ruralz_plugin_call_duration_seconds` bucket `le=\"0.00005\"` / `_count` | 99% (target) | 30 days | SM-6 (50 µs p99, target) |". Line 178: "`ruralz_plugin_call_duration_seconds` | Histogram, fast | seconds | `policy`, `phase` | SLI of SLO-GW-4". Vision SM-6: "WASM Plugin Phase call overhead, pooled instance, deadline interruption enabled, p99 | Per-Phase microbenchmark in CI | 50 µs or less (target)". Configuration model `geo-block`: "limits: {memoryBytes: 16Mi, timeout: 5ms}".
blocking.fix: Either (a) define the SLI as host overhead, for example a new `ruralz_plugin_call_overhead_seconds` (Histogram, fast; `policy`, `phase`) measured as the call time minus the time spent in guest code, and point SLO-GW-4 and SM-6 at it; or (b) keep `ruralz_plugin_call_duration_seconds`, drop the SM-6 tie, and set the objective per Plugin against its `limits.timeout`, proposed here.

blocking.section: Cardinality and overhead budgets (Overhead per signal)
blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 2 requires a per-signal overhead budget tagged (target). The CPU budgets for Metrics and Access log, the Metrics memory budget, the Access log allocation budget and the all-telemetry memory are tagged (hypothesis). These are estimates, not committed ceilings, so the two costliest signals have no (target) CPU budget.
blocking.evidence: Line 535: "| Metrics | 2 µs or less for 40 operations (hypothesis) | 0 (target) | 24 MiB or less at the series cap (hypothesis) |". Line 538: "| Access log, logged request | 2 µs or less at p99, `when` included (hypothesis) | 8 or fewer until a cel-go benchmark (hypothesis) | ...". Line 542: "| All telemetry at defaults | ... | 40 MiB or less (hypothesis) |". Manifest acceptance: "Cardinality and overhead budgets gives a per-signal overhead budget tagged (target)."
blocking.fix: Tag every budget cell (target): for example "2 µs or less for 40 operations (target)", "2 µs or less at p99 (target)", "8 or fewer (target)", "24 MiB or less (target)" and "40 MiB or less (target)". Move the supporting estimates (about 15 and 40 metric operations, 120 and 700 bytes per series) into the prose as (hypothesis), with the M1 benchmark that confirms or revises each target.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 457: "10 s (target), about one election timeout (hypothesis)" disagrees with Control plane and GitOps, which cites hashicorp/raft's 1000 ms default election timeout. Write "10 s (target), about ten default election timeouts", or derive the threshold from the configured election timeout.
Line 498: "nothing scrapes Nodes" contradicts Figure 1 and pack section 8.4, where a Prometheus-compatible scraper reads `/metrics` on 9901. Write "Ruralz Control never scrapes Nodes".

Line 208 limits `kind` on `ruralz_state_writes_dropped_total` to single-operation names, but Traffic management and resilience (line 365) proposes kind `cache_invalidate`. Accept it or reject it explicitly. Security and identity (line 113) also proposes a degraded reason for State Store URLs without credentials, which the Degraded states table does not list.

Line 136 says Multi-protocol's `ruralz_ingress_paused` and Traffic management's `ruralz_upstream_endpoint_ejections_total` are renamed. Multi-protocol already uses `ruralz_ingress_paused_partitions`, so drop that rename note. Traffic management still uses the old ejection name, so keep that one and have it resolved at conformance.

Option (c) "Ruralz encoders" of OQ-observability-16 would bypass the OpenTelemetry SDK for metrics, against pack section 7 and ADR-0010 ("OpenTelemetry-first (traces, metrics)"). Mark it "needs an ADR-0010 amendment". OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-16 names Observability as its owner, so the recommendation on line 45 should pick one of its listed options (OTel Prometheus exporter or Prometheus client) or say why neither fits.

Line 365 says "Histograms drop `route`; counters keep it", but `ruralz_ai_unpriced_requests_total`, `ruralz_ai_cache_markers_dropped_total`, `ruralz_ai_fallbacks_total`, `ruralz_ai_settlements_total` and `ruralz_ai_usage_missing_total` are counters without `route`. Reword the rule to match the table.

In the Configuration model, `headers-security` sets only response headers and `headers-internal` only request headers, yet Figure 2 draws `headers-security, onRequestHeaders` and two `headers-internal, onUpstreamResponseHeaders` spans. State whether a Phase with no operations still makes a call, or drop those three spans and recompute the figure of about 18 spans per trace and the budgets that depend on it. Listing the children in pack 8.12 Filter class order (cors, auth, authz, admission, transform) would also stop readers inferring a wrong order.
